title: Big-button TV companion
problem: People living with dementia (and exhausted caregivers) cannot operate modern smart TVs. Too many inputs, apps, PVR menus, and fragile remotes. They need power/volume/one favorite channel or one streaming destination with almost zero choices.
solution: A caregiver-configured TV companion: either (A) software+hub that locks a Fire TV / Android TV into a single destination with a 3-button physical remote enclosure, or (B) a simpler IR-only big-button path for non-streaming homes. Start with software config + 3D-printed remote shell; avoid medical claims.
whyWidespread: Repeated caregiver posts about TV/remote failure are extremely common. Existing products (Flipper, EZclicker, JubileeTV) prove willingness to pay, but leave gaps: streaming lock-down, caregiver remote config, and dementia-safe defaults.
targetUser: Adult children / spouses setting up TV for a person with moderate cognitive decline at home.
fitForGeorge: Software configuration UX + optional companion app + 3D-printed remote enclosure. Can assemble kits and sell direct/Amazon/Etsy without inventing new silicon.

feasibility.notes: Consumer electronics accessory + software. Avoid medical device framing. IR learning and Fire TV sideloading are the main tech risks.

market.willingnessToPay: Caregivers already pay $17-$40 for dumb big-button remotes and ~$200 for care systems. A $79-$149 configured kit is plausible.
market.profitHypothesis: Prototype BOM under ~$180 if using Fire TV Cube path; productized IR-only kit BOM can land under ~$35 with printed shell. Software differentiation + setup service is the margin story, not commodity remote plastic.

softwarePlan.summary: Caregiver web/app configures allowed destinations, volume ceiling, and power behavior. Device agent on Fire TV / Android TV enforces kiosk-like mode. Optional ESP/IR blaster path for dumb TVs.
mvpScope: One streaming destination or one input
Printed 3-button shell around a cheap remote or ESP input board
risks: Fire TV / Android TV policy changes blocking kiosk behavior
Support burden if every living room is different

solved: Need is repeatedly confirmed in dementia tech group
